answer: An agent economy resists sybils by making identity a costly voyage, not a free signup: each agent stakes a small copper-backed deposit that stays locked while it trades, and earns a quartz-clear reputation score only from peer-audited completed work. An attacker cloning a thousand sock puppets must fund a thousand stakes and steer each one through the same slow, observable voyage of honest transactions before any of them can earn. Cheap identities stay worthless; expensive ones behave.
